The test is: would a user fluent in the category's best tools (Linear, Figma, Notion, Raycast, Stripe come to mind) sit down and trust this interface, or pause at every subtly-off component?\n\nProduct UI's failure mode isn't flatness, it's strangeness without purpose: over-decorated buttons, mismatched form controls, gratuitous motion, display fonts where labels should be, invented affordances for standard tasks. The bar is earned familiarity. The tool should disappear into the task.\n\n## Typography\n\n- **System fonts are legitimate.** `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, \"Segoe UI\", system-ui, sans-serif` gives you native feel on every platform. Inter is the common cross-platform default for a reason.\n- **One family is often right.** Product UIs don't need display/body pairing. A well-tuned sans carries headings, buttons, labels, body, data.\n- **Fixed rem scale, not fluid.** Clamp-sized headings don't serve product UI. Users view at consistent DPI, and a fluid h1 that shrinks in a sidebar looks worse, not better.\n- **Tighter scale ratio.** 1.125–1.2 between steps is typical. More type elements here than on brand surfaces; exaggerated contrast creates noise.\n- **Line length still applies for prose** (65–75ch). Data and compact UI can run denser — tables at 120ch+ are fine.\n\n## Color\n\nProduct defaults to Restrained. A single surface can earn Committed — a dashboard where one category color carries a report, an onboarding flow with a drenched welcome screen — but Restrained is the floor.\n\n- State-rich semantic vocabulary: hover, focus, active, disabled, selected, loading, error, warning, success, info. Standardize these.\n- Accent color used for primary actions, current selection, and state indicators only — not decoration.\n- A second neutral layer for sidebars, toolbars, and panels (slightly cooler or warmer than the content surface).\n\n## Layout\n\n- Predictable grids. Consistency IS an affordance — users navigate faster when the structure is expected.\n- Familiar patterns are features. Standard navigation (top bar, side nav), breadcrumbs, tabs, and form layouts have established user expectations. Don't reinvent for flavor.\n- Responsive behavior is structural (collapse sidebar, responsive table, breakpoint-driven columns), not fluid typography.\n\n## Components\n\nEvery interactive component has: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error. Don't ship with half of these.\n\n- Skeleton states for loading, not spinners in the middle of content.\n- Empty states that teach the interface, not \"nothing here.\"\n- Consistent affordances across the surface. Same button shape. Same form-control vocabulary. Same icon style.\n\n## Motion\n\n- 150–250 ms on most transitions. Users are in flow — don't make them wait for choreography.\n- Motion conveys state, not decoration. State change, feedback, loading, reveal — nothing else.\n- No orchestrated page-load sequences. Product loads into a task; users don't want to watch it load.\n\n## Product bans (on top of the shared absolute bans)\n\n- Decorative motion that doesn't convey state.\n- Inconsistent component vocabulary across screens. If the \"save\" button looks different in two places, one is wrong.\n- Display fonts in UI labels, buttons, data.\n- Reinventing standard affordances for flavor (custom scrollbars, weird form controls, non-standard modals).\n- Heavy color or full-saturation accents on inactive states.\n\n## Product permissions\n\nProduct can afford things brand surfaces can't.\n\n- System fonts and familiar sans defaults (Inter, SF Pro, system-ui stacks).\n- Standard navigation patterns: top bar + side nav, breadcrumbs, tabs, command palettes.\n- Density. Tables with many rows, panels with many labels, dense information when users need it.\n- Consistency over surprise. The same visual vocabulary screen to screen is a virtue; delight is saved for moments, not pages.\n# Teach Flow\n\nGathers design context for a project and writes two complementary files at the project root:\n\n- **PRODUCT.md** (strategic): register, target users, product purpose, brand personality, anti-references, strategic design principles. Answers \"who/what/why\".\n- **DESIGN.md** (visual): visual theme, color palette, typography, components, layout. Follows the [Google Stitch DESIGN.md format](https://stitch.withgoogle.com/docs/design-md/format/). Answers \"how it looks\".\n\nEvery other impeccable command reads these files before doing any work.\n\n## Step 1: Load current state\n\nRun the shared loader first so you know what already exists:\n\n```bash\nnode .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/load-context.mjs\n```\n\nThe output tells you whether PRODUCT.md and/or DESIGN.md already exist. If `migrated: true`, legacy `.impeccable.md` was auto-renamed to `PRODUCT.md`. Mention this once to the user.\n\nDecision tree:\n- **Neither file exists (empty project or no context yet)**: do Steps 2-4 (write PRODUCT.md), then decide on DESIGN.md based on whether there's code to analyze.\n- **PRODUCT.md exists, DESIGN.md missing**: skip to Step 5 — offer to run `$impeccable document` for DESIGN.md.\n- **PRODUCT.md exists but has no `## Register` section (legacy)**: add it. Infer a hypothesis from the codebase (see Step 2), confirm with the user, write the field.\n- **Both exist**: ask the user directly to clarify what you cannot infer. which to refresh. Skip the one the user doesn't want changed.\n- **Just DESIGN.md exists (unusual)**: do Steps 2-4 to produce PRODUCT.md.\n\nNever silently overwrite an existing file. Always confirm first.\n\n## Step 2: Explore the codebase\n\nBefore asking questions, thoroughly scan the project to discover what you can:\n\n- **README and docs**: Project purpose, target audience, any stated goals\n- **Package.json / config files**: Tech stack, dependencies, existing design libraries\n- **Existing components**: Current design patterns, spacing, typography in use\n- **Brand assets**: Logos, favicons, color values already defined\n- **Design tokens / CSS variables**: Existing color palettes, font stacks, spacing scales\n- **Any style guides or brand documentation**\n\nAlso form a **register hypothesis** from what you find:\n\n- Brand signals: `/`, `/about`, `/pricing`, `/blog/*`, `/docs/*`, hero sections, big typography, scroll-driven sections, landing-page-shaped content.\n- Product signals: `/app/*`, `/dashboard`, `/settings`, `/(auth)`, forms, data tables, side/top nav, app-shell components.\n\nRegister is a hypothesis at this point, not a decision — Step 3 confirms it.\n\nNote what you've learned and what remains unclear. This exploration feeds both PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md.\n\n## Step 3: Ask strategic questions (for PRODUCT.md)\n\nask the user directly to clarify what you cannot infer. Focus only on what you couldn't infer from the codebase.\n\n### Register (ask first — it shapes everything below)\n\nEvery design task is either **brand** (marketing, landing, campaign, long-form content, portfolio — design IS the product) or **product** (app UI, admin, dashboards, tools — design SERVES the product).\n\nIf Step 2 produced a clear hypothesis, lead with it: *\"From the codebase, this looks like a [brand / product] surface — does that match your intent, or should we treat it differently?\"*\n\nIf the signal is genuinely split (e.g. a product with a big marketing landing), ask the user directly to clarify what you cannot infer. which register describes the **primary** surface. The register can be overridden per task later, but PRODUCT.md carries one default.\n\n### Users & Purpose\n- Who uses this? What's their context when using it?\n- What job are they trying to get done?\n- For brand: what emotions should the interface evoke? (confidence, delight, calm, urgency)\n- For product: what workflow are they in? What's the primary task on any given screen?\n\n### Brand & Personality\n- How would you describe the brand personality in 3 words?\n- Reference sites or apps that capture the right feel? What specifically about them?\n  - For brand, push for real-world references in the right lane (tech-minimal, editorial-magazine, consumer-warm, brutalist-grid, etc.) — not generic \"modern\" adjectives.\n  - For product, push for category best-tool references (Linear, Figma, Notion, Raycast, Stripe).\n- What should this explicitly NOT look like? Any anti-references?\n\n### Accessibility & Inclusion\n- Specific accessibility requirements? (WCAG level, known user needs)\n- Considerations for reduced motion, color blindness, or other accommodations?\n\nSkip questions where the answer is already clear. **Do NOT ask about colors, fonts, radii, or visual styling here** — those belong in DESIGN.md, not PRODUCT.md.\n\n## Step 4: Write PRODUCT.md\n\nSynthesize into a strategic document:\n\n```markdown\n# Product\n\n## Register\n\nproduct\n\n## Users\n[Who they are, their context, the job to be done]\n\n## Product Purpose\n[What this product does, why it exists, what success looks like]\n\n## Brand Personality\n[Voice, tone, 3-word personality, emotional goals]\n\n## Anti-references\n[What this should NOT look like. Specific bad-example sites or patterns to avoid.]\n\n## Design Principles\n[3-5 strategic principles derived from the conversation. Principles like \"practice what you preach\", \"show, don't tell\", \"expert confidence\" — NOT visual rules like \"use OKLCH\" or \"magenta accent\".]\n\n## Accessibility & Inclusion\n[WCAG level, known user needs, considerations]\n```\n\nRegister is either `brand` or `product` as a bare value. No prose, no commentary.\n\nWrite to `PROJECT_ROOT/PRODUCT.md`. If `.impeccable.md` existed, the loader already renamed it — merge into that content rather than starting from scratch.\n\n## Step 5: Decide on DESIGN.md\n\nOffer `$impeccable document` either way. Two paths:\n\n- **Code exists** (CSS tokens, components, a running site): \"I can generate a DESIGN.md that captures your visual system (colors, typography, components) so variants stay on-brand. Want to do that now?\"\n- **Pre-implementation** (empty project): \"I can seed a starter DESIGN.md from five quick questions about color strategy, type direction, motion energy, and references. You can re-run once there's code, to capture the real tokens. Want to do that now?\"\n\nIf the user agrees, delegate to `$impeccable document` (it auto-detects scan vs seed). Load its reference and follow that flow.\n\nIf the user prefers to skip, mention they can run `$impeccable document` any time later.\n\n## Step 6: Confirm and wrap up\n\nSummarize:\n- Register captured (brand / product)\n- What was written (PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, or both)\n- The 3-5 strategic principles from PRODUCT.md that will guide future work\n- If DESIGN.md is pending, remind the user how to generate it later\n\n**Critical: re-run the loader to refresh session context.** After writing PRODUCT.md, run `node .agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/load-context.mjs` one final time and let its full JSON output land in conversation. This ensures subsequent commands in this session use the freshly-written PRODUCT.md, not a stale earlier version.\n\nIf teach was invoked as a blocker by another impeccable command (e.g. the user ran `$impeccable polish` with no PRODUCT.md), resume that original task now with the fresh context.\n\nOptionally ask the user directly to clarify what you cannot infer. whether they'd like a brief summary of PRODUCT.md appended to AGENTS.md for easier agent reference. If yes, append a short **Design Context** pointer section there.\n"
  }
]

## Codex final · 2026-07-11T12:20:48.385Z

You found the actual root cause. The backend captured Claude’s `AskUserQuestion`, but the conversation timeline silently ignored `elicitation` entries. The answer UI existed only inside the optional worker sidebar.

The audit also found broader gaps:

| Claude capability | Current state |
|---|---|
| `AskUserQuestion` | Persisted, but missing from the main conversation |
| Permissions / `ExitPlanMode` | Sidebar-only; timeline is non-actionable |
| TODO/task plans | Claude emits them; runtime drops them |
| Slash commands | Claude emits availability; runtime drops it |
| Interactive/background terminals | Not negotiated; reduced to fallback output |
| Mode/config/session updates | Mostly dropped |
| Reads, writes, images, MCP servers | Already supported |
| Tool calls, results, diffs | Supported, but without an exhaustive compatibility contract |

The underlying risk is version drift: OmniHarness uses ACP SDK `0.14.1`, while the installed Claude adapter uses ACP SDK `0.25.0`. Elicitation was manually patched through an extension method, which is how this became half-implemented.

My recommended design is a complete Claude adapter contract:

- Upgrade OmniHarness to the adapter’s ACP protocol version.
- Render questions and permission decisions inline where the agent stops, not behind a sidebar.
- Support every form field Claude can emit: choices, multiple choices, text, numbers, booleans, required fields, descriptions, and custom answers.
- Preserve pending interactions through reload, reconnect, and recovery.
- Handle plans/TODOs, slash commands, mode changes, session metadata, and terminal output.
- Keep the worker sidebar as a secondary control surface.
- Add a compatibility test that fails whenever Claude advertises or emits a request/update OmniHarness does not handle.
- Add lifecycle scenarios proving question selection, permission decisions, plan-mode exit, reconnect, and continued output end to end.

One scope decision before I write the specification: should I implement the complete production surface used by Claude Code (recommended), or also implement experimental ACP 0.25 features Claude Code does not currently depend on, such as provider management, next-edit suggestions, and ACP-over-MCP?

Get git SHAs:**\n```bash\nBASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or origin/main\nHEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)\n```\n\n**2. Dispatch code-reviewer subagent:**\n\nUse Task tool with ultrapowers:code-reviewer type, fill template at `code-reviewer.md`\n\n**Placeholders:**\n- `{WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED}` - What you just built\n- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do\n- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit\n- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit\n- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary\n\n**3. Act on feedback:**\n- Fix Critical issues immediately\n- Fix Important issues before proceeding\n- Note Minor issues for later\n- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)\n\n## Example\n\n```\n[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]\n\nYou: Let me request code review before proceeding.\n\nBASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep \"Task 1\" | head -1 | awk '{print $1}')\nHEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)\n\n[Dispatch ultrapowers:code-reviewer subagent]\n  WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED: Verification and repair functions for conversation index\n  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/superpowers/plans/deployment-plan.md\n  BASE_SHA: a7981ec\n  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661\n  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types\n\n[Subagent returns]:\n  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests\n  Issues:\n    Important: Missing progress indicators\n    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval\n  Assessment: Ready to proceed\n\nYou: [Fix progress indicators]\n[Continue to Task 3]\n```\n\n## Integration with Workflows\n\n**Subagent-Driven Development:**\n- Review after EACH task\n- Catch issues before they compound\n- Fix before moving to next task\n\n**Executing Plans:**\n- Review after each batch (3 tasks)\n- Get feedback, apply, continue\n\n**Ad-Hoc Development:**\n- Review before merge\n- Review when stuck\n\n## Red Flags\n\n**Never:**\n- Skip review because \"it's simple\"\n- Ignore Critical issues\n- Proceed with unfixed Important issues\n- Argue with valid technical feedback\n\n**If reviewer wrong:**\n- Push back with technical reasoning\n- Show code/tests that prove it works\n- Request clarification\n\nSee template at: requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md\n"

## Codex progress · 2026-07-11T12:24:30.820Z

The scope is now fixed: production Claude Code support first, then every ACP 0.25 client/agent capability, including experimental provider, next-edit, elicitation URL, plan, and MCP-over-ACP features. I’m writing the durable protocol contract and executable plan now; nothing will be considered supported merely because it parses. Each advertised capability must have persistence, a usable surface or API, lifecycle events, and tests.

Claude Code must never block on an interaction the conversation cannot display, and no ACP 0.25 request, notification, session update, capability, or content type may be silently dropped.\n+\n+## Incident\n+\n+Session `0abd06014635` emitted a valid Claude Code `AskUserQuestion` tool call followed by an ACP form elicitation containing selectable answers. The runtime persisted both records, but the main conversation renderer ignored `elicitation` entries. The only actionable form lived in the optional worker sidebar. The conversation therefore appeared stuck while the agent correctly waited for input.\n+\n+The audit found a protocol-version mismatch behind this partial implementation: OmniHarness is compiled against `@agentclientprotocol/sdk@0.14.1`, while the installed Claude adapter uses ACP SDK `0.25.0`. Elicitation was manually routed through `extMethod`, and several newer session updates and capabilities were never modeled.\n+\n+## Users and Jobs\n+\n+The primary user is a human supervising coding agents from the main conversation.\n+\n+- When an agent asks a question, the user answers at the exact point where execution paused.\n+- When an agent requests permission or a mode change, the user sees the operation, every offered decision, and its consequences.\n+- When an agent emits plans, tasks, terminal sessions, diffs, commands, media, resources, or session changes, the user can inspect the real state without opening a debugging panel.\n+- After reload, reconnect, server restart, or worker recovery, pending actions remain actionable exactly once.\n+- Operators and tests can inspect every protocol decision through named events and persisted streams.\n+\n+## Product Principles\n+\n+1. **The conversation is the primary control surface.** Worker sidebars may mirror actions, but they may not be the only place to continue a blocked turn.\n+2. **Advertised means operational.** OmniHarness advertises a capability only when its request handling, persistence, user/API surface, error behavior, and tests are complete.\n+3. **Unknown means visible failure.** Unknown standard ACP methods or session updates emit typed compatibility errors; they are never ignored.\n+4. **One persisted worker stream.** Protocol output and human-input state remain in the existing append-only worker JSONL. No parallel transcript store is introduced.\n+5. **Stable identity and exactly-once decisions.** Requests use stable session/request/tool-call identifiers. Replays and duplicate responses cannot answer a different or already-settled request.\n+6. **Protocol data is stored, UI copy is translated at render time.** No translated strings are persisted.\n+\n+## Protocol Baseline\n+\n+OmniHarness will compile against `@agentclientprotocol/sdk@0.25.0`, matching the Claude adapter. The dependency is pinned to an exact compatible version and covered by a schema contract test.\n+\n+The compatibility gate reads the installed SDK schema and asserts that every standard ACP 0.25 method, notification, session-update discriminator, content type, and advertised capability is classified as one of:\n+\n+- fully handled and advertised;\n+- fully handled but intentionally not advertised for a specific surface;\n+- explicitly rejected with a typed `error.surfaced` compatibility event.\n+\n+The test fails when a future SDK adds an unclassified protocol member.\n+\n+## Phase 1: Claude Code Complete Surface\n+\n+### Inline human input\n+\n+Add `elicitation` as a first-class `AgentActivityItem`. Pending form elicitations render inline in `Terminal` between the initiating tool call and later activity. The form supports ACP 0.25 property schemas:\n+\n+- strings and free text;\n+- titled `enum`, `oneOf`, and multi-select options;\n+- booleans;\n+- integers and numbers with min/max constraints;\n+- required and optional fields;\n+- field titles and descriptions;\n+- custom-answer fields;\n+- accept, decline, and cancel outcomes.\n+\n+Single-choice questions render as immediately scannable choices rather than a closed native select. Multi-select questions render as checkboxes. Free text uses the existing shadcn textarea/input controls. The pending form is expanded by default and remains visible after reload.\n+\n+Permission requests become first-class inline actions as well. Every adapter-provided `PermissionOption` is rendered verbatim by stable `optionId`; OmniHarness does not collapse `allow_once`, `allow_always`, `reject_once`, or plan-mode choices into generic Yes/No controls. The action includes the tool title, kind, affected file/command where available, and any diff or plan content.\n+\n+The sidebar reuses the same field parser, decision model, validation, and translated controls. It is a mirror, not a separate implementation.\n+\n+### Ownership and state\n+\n+- Server authority: pending permission and elicitation records on the live runtime plus pending entries reconstructed from the unified worker stream.\n+- Stable token: [REDACTED] + requestId + toolCallId`.\n+- Ordering: worker stream `seq`.\n+- Terminal states: answered/approved/denied/declined/cancelled/failed.\n+- Draft owner: a dedicated global interaction manager keyed by the stable request token; only the small inline form subscribes to its draft slice.\n+- Mutation ownership: a response may settle only the exact still-pending request token. Late success/error callbacks cannot modify another run or request.\n+- Persistence: pending protocol records and terminal outcome records remain in the worker stream; draft form text is intentionally browser-memory only and clears on settlement or navigation.\n+\n+### Claude output completeness\n+\n+Handle and expose every feature claimed by the installed Claude adapter:\n+\n+- text and image prompts;\n+- generic tool calls and results;\n+- permissions and `ExitPlanMode` decisions;\n+- `AskUserQuestion` and MCP form elicitation;\n+- edit/write diffs;\n+- TODO and Task plan updates;\n+- Bash interactive/background terminal output and cancellation;\n+- available slash commands;\n+- mode and configuration changes;\n+- session metadata and usage;\n+- client MCP servers;\n+- load, resume, fork, close, and delete session operations supported by the adapter.\n+\n+## Phase 2: Full ACP 0.25 Client\n+\n+### Agent-to-client requests\n+\n+Implement every standard request in the ACP 0.25 `AgentRequest` union:\n+\n+- `fs/read_text_file` and `fs/write_text_file` with workspace-bound path validation and named failure events;\n+- `session/request_permission`;\n+- `terminal/create`, `terminal/output`, `terminal/wait_for_exit`, `terminal/kill`, and `terminal/release` using a server-owned terminal manager with bounded output, cancellation, cleanup, and persisted tool metadata;\n+- `elicitation/create` for form and URL modes, including URL completion notifications;\n+- `mcp/connect`, `mcp/message`, and `mcp/disconnect` using connection-scoped ownership and cleanup;\n+- extension requests through an explicit registry. Unknown extensions return method-not-found and emit `acp.compatibility_unsupported`.\n+\n+### Agent-to-client notifications\n+\n+Handle all ACP 0.25 notifications:\n+\n+- `session/update`;\n+- `elicitation/complete`;\n+- MCP messages;\n+- registered extension notifications.\n+\n+### Session updates\n+\n+Persist or project every `SessionUpdate` variant:\n+\n+- user, agent, and thought content chunks;\n+- tool calls and updates;\n+- plan, plan update, and plan removed;\n+- available commands;\n+- current mode;\n+- configuration options;\n+- session information;\n+- usage and cost.\n+\n+Unknown discriminators emit a compatibility failure and mark the runtime snapshot degraded instead of disappearing.\n+\n+### Content and tool-call content\n+\n+Support every ACP content block and tool-call content variant: text, image, audio, embedded text/blob resources, resource links, diffs, terminals, and nested content. Binary payloads are bounded and represented by durable metadata or existing attachment storage, never expanded into unbounded SSE snapshots.\n+\n+### Client capabilities\n+\n+Implement and truthfully negotiate all ACP 0.25 `ClientCapabilities`:\n+\n+- auth environment-variable and terminal flows;\n+- form and URL elicitation;\n+- filesystem read/write;\n+- next-edit document/context capabilities;\n+- structured plan updates;\n+- position encodings;\n+- terminal operations.\n+\n+### Agent capabilities and client-originated methods\n+\n+Expose all ACP 0.25 agent capabilities through typed runtime methods and appropriate product surfaces or scriptable APIs:\n+\n+- authentication, provider listing/selection/disable/logout;\n+- session new/load/list/resume/fork/close/delete;\n+- modes and configuration options;\n+- prompt and cancel;\n+- next-edit start/suggest/close plus document/open/focus/change/save notifications;\n+- MCP-over-ACP messaging;\n+- extension registry.\n+\n+Provider, session, and next-edit operations use Manager-owned client state, stable operation tokens, named events, and full backend error details.\n+\n+## UI Surfaces\n+\n+### Conversation timeline\n+\n+Pending human input is placed inline and expanded. It uses the current restrained visual system, clear warning/attention semantics, keyboard-focus rings, and `aria-live` status updates. Settled interactions collapse to compact historical rows that state the outcome without exposing secret values.\n+\n+### Composer\n+\n+Available ACP slash commands feed a command menu owned by a dedicated manager. Commands remain scoped to the selected live session and cannot leak across navigation.\n+\n+### Plans and tasks\n+\n+ACP plans/tasks render in the conversation as structured progress, distinct from Omni supervisor planning artifacts. Updates merge by stable plan/task ID and sequence; removals are explicit.\n+\n+### Terminal output\n+\n+Bash tool rows embed bounded live terminal output and expose stop/cancel only while the corresponding process is active. Terminal resource cleanup is server-owned and observable.\n+\n+### Provider, session, and next-edit surfaces\n+\n+Provider/session operations reuse existing settings and conversation controls where they naturally belong. Next-edit suggestions integrate with project-file viewing rather than creating a fake editor. Scriptable HTTP endpoints remain available for capabilities without a permanently visible control.\n+\n+## Observability\n+\n+Add named events for:\n+\n+- `acp.request_received`, `acp.request_completed`, `acp.request_failed`;\n+- `acp.compatibility_unsupported`;\n+- `worker.elicitation_requested`, `worker.elicitation_answered`, `worker.elicitation_declined`, `worker.elicitation_cancelled`;\n+- `worker.permission_requested` and terminal permission outcomes;\n+- terminal created/exited/killed/released;\n+- MCP connected/disconnected/failed;\n+- plan updated/removed;\n+- provider/session/NES operations and failures.\n+\n+User-relevant failures also emit `error.surfaced` with stable codes and run/worker/session ownership.\n+\n+## Error and Security Requirements\n+\n+- Filesystem operations are restricted to the agent session workspace and explicitly attached additional directories.\n+- URL elicitation uses an allowlisted browser/open-URL flow and never auto-completes from an untrusted page.\n+- Terminal commands inherit the worker environment but never expose secret environment values in output metadata.\n+- MCP connections are bounded per agent session and closed on cancellation, agent exit, or server shutdown.\n+- Provider authentication values are never persisted in worker output or frontend state.\n+- Unknown protocol input is preserved in diagnostic previews with size limits, while full secret-bearing payloads are not logged.\n+\n+## Testing\n+\n+### Deterministic tests\n+\n+- Schema compatibility test for every ACP 0.25 union member.\n+- Runtime request/notification tests for every agent-to-client method.\n+- Session-update round-trip tests for every discriminator and content type.\n+- Worker-stream reconstruction tests for pending and settled interactions.\n+- React activity/model tests for elicitation, permissions, plans, commands, terminals, and media.\n+- Mutation ownership tests for navigation, replay, duplicate response, and stale callbacks.\n+- Locale parity tests.\n+- Hot-path tests proving pending forms and terminal updates do not trigger whole-app per-keystroke rendering or unbounded snapshots.\n+\n+### Lifecycle scenarios\n+\n+- Claude asks a multi-choice question; the main conversation displays it; the selected answer reaches Claude; Claude continues.\n+- Reload while a question or permission is pending; the same request reappears exactly once and remains actionable.\n+- Exit-plan-mode options preserve their exact IDs and selected mode.\n+- Disconnect/reconnect replays plan, terminal, permission, and elicitation events without duplication.\n+- Server restart cleans up or reattaches terminal and MCP resources with named decisions.\n+- Unknown future method/update produces an explicit compatibility failure.\n+\n+### Product verification\n+\n+Use the already-running application for browser verification. Verify desktop and narrow/mobile layouts, keyboard-only completion, focus retention, visible loading/error/settled states, and that typing in a pending answer does not repaint the conversation shell. Approval-gated agentic journey testing may be proposed separately; deterministic browser and lifecycle coverage is required regardless.\n+\n+## Acceptance Criteria\n+\n+1. The exact question from session `0abd06014635` renders inline with its four choices and custom-answer field when replayed as a fixture.\n+2. A user can answer every Claude Code permission and elicitation without opening the worker sidebar.\n+3. Every feature claimed by the installed Claude adapter is handled end to end.\n+4. Every ACP 0.25 standard method, notification, session update, content variant, and capability is classified by an executable compatibility test.\n+5. OmniHarness never advertises an incomplete capability.\n+6. Reload, reconnect, recovery, duplication, and stale-response tests pass.\n+7. All user-facing copy is translated through every locale resource.\n+8. Typecheck, lint, focused tests, lifecycle tests, build, and live product verification pass.\n+\n*** End Patch";

Testing the inline elicitation UI in Task 3 is impossible without the corresponding backend request handler to receive, validate, and respond to the elicitation.\\n10. **Unsafe Settle Sequence**: Define a transaction-safe database/stream sequence for settling interactions: persist the user's answer in SQLite and append the outcome to the worker JSONL stream *first* before sending the JSON-RPC response to the Agent, to prevent inconsistent states if the Agent call fails or the server crashes mid-flight.\\n11. **Fragile Draft State Ownership**: Persist user drafts in browser `localStorage` (keyed by the stable request token) instead of relying on memory-only drafts in `AgentInteractionManager.ts`. When a skill or prompt says to use `node_repl`, call this server's `js` execution tool. Calls default to a 30000 ms (30 seconds) timeout when `timeout_ms` is omitted. The runtime exposes `nodeRepl.cwd`, `nodeRepl.homeDir`, `nodeRepl.tmpDir`, `nodeRepl.requestMeta`, `nodeRepl.setResponseMeta(...)`, and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(...)`. Top-level bindings persist across `js` calls until `js_reset`; do not redeclare existing `const` or `let` names. Reuse existing bindings, use top-level `var` for reusable state that may be assigned again, or choose a fresh descriptive name. Use `js_add_node_module_dir` before `js` when a skill provides an extra package directory, and use dynamic imports like `await import(\\\"playwright\\\")` rather than filesystem paths under `./node_modules`.\\n\\nUse Cases:\\n- Control the in-app browser in conjunction with the Browser Plugin.\\n- Control the Chrome browser in conjunction with the Chrome Plugin. Prefer this method of controlling Chrome over alternatives (such as Computer Use) unless the user explicitly mentions an alternative.\\n- Control desktop apps on macOS through Computer Use.\\n\\nRun JavaScript in a persistent Node-backed kernel with top-level await. This is the JavaScript execution tool for the `node_repl` MCP server; use it whenever instructions say to use `node_repl`, the Node REPL MCP, or run Node REPL code. If `timeout_ms` is omitted, execution times out after 30000 ms (30 seconds); pass a larger `timeout_ms` for slow browser automation or other long-running operations. Use `nodeRepl.cwd`, `nodeRepl.homeDir`, and `nodeRepl.tmpDir` to inspect host paths. Use `nodeRepl.requestMeta` to inspect the current MCP request `_meta` object during a tool call. Use `nodeRepl.setResponseMeta(meta)` to attach top-level MCP result `_meta`; repeated calls shallow-merge object keys for the current tool call. Use `nodeRepl.write(value)` to add output without a newline. Strings are unchanged; other values use console-style formatting, including BigInt and circular objects. Prefer it over `console.log(...)` for final output; `console.log(...)` remains useful for debugging or multiple values. Use `await nodeRepl.emitImage(imageLike)` to return images; each call adds one image to the outer tool result, so call it multiple times to emit multiple images. Supported image inputs are a data URL, inferred PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes, or `{ bytes, mimeType }`. Saved references to `nodeRepl.write(...)` and `nodeRepl.emitImage(...)` stay reusable across calls, but async callbacks that fire after a call finishes still fail because no exec is active. Top-level bindings persist across calls until `js_reset`. If a call throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain reusable. For reusable names that may be assigned again later, prefer top-level `var name = ...`; `var` can be redeclared across calls. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, reuse the existing binding if possible, reassign it only if it was declared with `let` or `var`, or pick a new name instead of resetting immediately; a previous `const x` cannot be changed into `var x`. Use a short `{ ... }` block only for temporary scratch names, and do not wrap an entire call in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Use dynamic imports like `await import(\\\"playwright\\\")`, `await import(\\\"pkg\\\")`, or `await import(\\\"./file.js\\\")`; top-level static `import` is not supported. Import packages by package name after installing them into a directory added with `js_add_node_module_dir`, `NODE_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, or the working directory. Do not import package entrypoints by filesystem path such as `./node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`. Imported local files must be ESM `.js` or `.mjs` files and run in the context chosen at their dynamic-import boundary, so they can also use `nodeRepl.*`, the captured `console`, and `import.meta` helpers. Bare package imports always resolve from the REPL-wide search roots (`NODE_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, then directories later added with `js_add_node_module_dir`, then cwd), not relative to the imported file's location. Imported local files may statically import other local `.js` / `.mjs` files, available packages, and allowed Node builtins. `import.meta.resolve()` returns importable strings such as `file://...`, bare package names, and `node:...` specifiers. Local file modules reload between execs. `node:` builtins are generally available via dynamic import, but `process` / `node:process` remains blocked for now because the current Rust-server-to-Node-child transport runs over stdio and raw process streams can corrupt it. Prefer `nodeRepl.write(...)` for text or formatted values and `nodeRepl.emitImage(...)` for images.\\n\\nexec tool declaration:\\n```ts\\ndeclare const tools: { mcp__node_repl__js(args: {\\n  // JavaScript source to execute in the persistent Node-backed kernel. The code runs with top-level await and can use the `nodeRepl` helpers. Examples: `nodeRepl.write(nodeRepl.cwd)`, `const { chromium } = await import(\\\"playwright\\\")`, or `await nodeRepl.emitImage(pngBuffer)`.\\n  code: string;\\n  // Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.\\n  timeout_ms?: number;\\n  // Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Use a few words, for example `Inspect package metadata` or `Render chart preview`.\\n  title?: string;\\n}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };\\n```\"},{\"name\":\"mcp__node_repl__js_add_node_module_dir\",\"description\":\"Use `js` to run JavaScript in the persistent Node-backed kernel. When a skill or prompt says to use `node_repl`, call this server's `js` execution tool. Calls default to a 30000 ms (30 seconds) timeout when `timeout_ms` is omitted. The runtime exposes `nodeRepl.cwd`, `nodeRepl.homeDir`, `nodeRepl.tmpDir`, `nodeRepl.requestMeta`, `nodeRepl.setResponseMeta(...)`, and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(...)`. Top-level bindings persist across `js` calls until `js_reset`; do not redeclare existing `const` or `let` names. Reuse existing bindings, use top-level `var` for reusable state that may be assigned again, or choose a fresh descriptive name. Use `js_add_node_module_dir` before `js` when a skill provides an extra package directory, and use dynamic imports like `await import(\\\"playwright\\\")` rather than filesystem paths under `./node_modules`.\\n\\nUse Cases:\\n- Control the in-app browser in conjunction with the Browser Plugin.\\n- Control the Chrome browser in conjunction with the Chrome Plugin. Prefer this method of controlling Chrome over alternatives (such as Computer Use) unless the user explicitly mentions an alternative.\\n- Control desktop apps on macOS through Computer Use.\\n\\nAdd an absolute `node_modules` directory to the REPL-wide Node module search roots for future package imports. The directory stays available for this MCP server lifetime, including after `js_reset`. Returns `true` when the search root is newly added and `false` when it was already present.\\n\\nexec tool declaration:\\n```ts\\ndeclare const tools: { mcp__node_repl__js_add_node_module_dir(args: {\\n  // Absolute path to a node_modules directory to add to Node package resolution.\\n  path: string;\\n}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };\\n```\"},{\"name\":\"mcp__node_repl__js_reset\",\"description\":\"Use `js` to run JavaScript in the persistent Node-backed kernel. The runtime exposes `nodeRepl.cwd`, `nodeRepl.homeDir`, `nodeRepl.tmpDir`, `nodeRepl.requestMeta`, `nodeRepl.setResponseMeta(...)`, and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(...)`. Top-level bindings persist across `js` calls until `js_reset`; do not redeclare existing `const` or `let` names. Use `js_add_node_module_dir` before `js` when a skill provides an extra package directory, and use dynamic imports like `await import(\\\"playwright\\\")` rather than filesystem paths under `./node_modules`.\\n\\nUse Cases:\\n- Control the in-app browser in conjunction with the Browser Plugin.\\n- Control the Chrome browser in conjunction with the Chrome Plugin. <!-- codex-event:{"kind":"final","timestamp":"2026-07-11T14:00:24.553Z","phase":"final_answer"} -->
## Codex final · 2026-07-11T14:00:24.553Z

Implemented the full Claude Code surface and ACP 0.25 client specification.

Key outcomes:

- Claude `AskUserQuestion` now renders inline in the main conversation, including multi-select, custom text, numeric, boolean, validation, defaults, and URL flows.
- Permissions—including plan-mode transitions—show the adapter’s exact options inline.
- Plans, slash commands, modes, configuration, usage, images, audio, resources, diffs, and bounded terminal output are persisted and rendered.
- All 42 ACP methods are covered: filesystem, terminals, MCP, providers, sessions, auth, NES/document events, cancellation, and extensions.
- Responses are request-ID guarded, reload-safe, and persisted before unblocking the agent.
- The earlier UI request loop/read-marker slowdown is fixed.
- Added the authenticated `/api/agents/:name/acp` endpoint.
- Added the incident regression and lifecycle replay tests.

Verification:

- 101 focused tests passed.
- TypeScript and targeted lint passed.
- Production build passed.
- ACP compatibility check passed: 42/42 methods.
- Live app returns `200`; ACP endpoint is mounted and authentication-protected.
- Independent final review: `READY`.

The full repository suite still has 36 unrelated failures across existing failover, queue, output-archive, and lifecycle tests; the complete affected test set is green.

Main implementation: [runtime-client.ts](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/agent-runtime/acp/runtime-client.ts), [InlineElicitation.tsx](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/agent-interactions/InlineElicitation.tsx), [ConversationMain.tsx](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/home/ConversationMain.tsx), and the [incident learning note](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/docs/superpowers/learnings/2026-07-11-hidden-acp-interaction.md).
